question: Which V2O5 film thicknesses were tested electrochemically, how many ALD cycles gave the thicker film, and did the potential shifts differ between them?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE regexp_matches(text, '(?i)(nm|cycle|thick|shift|voltammet|CV)') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (4,5) ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE regexp_matches(text, '(?i)(ALD|cycles|40 nm|80 nm|1000|500|2000|nm\b)') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (2,3,6) AND line_no BETWEEN 1 AND 100 ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (6,7) AND line_no BETWEEN 60 AND 140 ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE (page=7 AND line_no BETWEEN 40 AND 60) OR (page=1) ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT figure_id, line_no, text FROM figure_ocr WHERE figure_id IN ('p2.F1','p3.F2','p5.F4') ORDER BY figure_id, line_no

rendered:
The electrochemically tested V2O5 films were the ∼80 nm[1] film and the ∼40 nm[2] film. The thicker of these, the ∼80 nm[3] film, was deposited with 1000 ALD cycles[4]. The document does not state the ALD cycle count used for the thinner film.

The potential shifts were similar for both films: strain produced a shift of about ∼40 mV[5] in both, and similar shifts in values of ΔEeq(avg) were observed[6], owing to the similar locked-in elastic strains.
